title.narrative: Save Lives of Conflict Affected Children Suffering from Acute Malnutrition in Adamawa and Borno States Through Access to Quality Nutrition Services

description.narrative: ltpgtGZDI GEEWCI are jointly proposing a lifesaving nutrition project targeted to provide lifesaving nutrition services and assistance to directly 4,720 conflict affected populations in Adamawa and Borno states, Northeast Nigeria. The project targets to reach 15% persons with disabilities in line with the IASC guidelines for inclusion of persons with disabilities and an estimated 23,600 indirect beneficiaries. The project is proposed to be implemented in the highly prioritized LGAs of Michika of Adamawa State and Nganzai of Borno State. Notably, the project needs a total of overall budget of US$100,000 to urgently provide the highly needed and strategic results designed into the following complementary outcomes: ltbrgtltbgtltbrgtlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtOutcome 1lt/bgt of the project seeks to enhance well-being of conflict affected children and their families, pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls and other at-risks groups through promoting access to quality and comprehensive curative services by strengthening early identification of cases, strengthening referrals and community-based management of acute malnutrition. Under this outcome, GZDI GEEWCI focused to facilitate community-based screening of 2000 children and children with disability for acute malnutrition, refer and provide community-based treatment of moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) to children through targeted supplementary feeding programme or tom brown. Children with severe acute malnutrition are further targeted for quality, adequate and comprehensive treatment as well as PBWGs with MAM conditions will be supported to have access to community-based treatment that enhance their recovery and living conditions. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtOutcome 2lt/bgt of the project aimed to deliver quality preventative nutrition assistance and services to conflict affected children, families and the wider community members by urgently providing supplemental nutrition assistance or supplementary feeding, appropriate maternal, infant and young child feeding including micronutrient for children under 5 and pregnant, breastfeeding women and girls. This outcome will reach children, PBWGs, caregivers and the wider community members with preventative services and assistance. More specifically, children age 6-23 months will receive MNPs/SQ-LNS, PBWG will benefit from SNAs, caregivers and PBWGs will received quality and comprehensive skilled MIYCN support/counseling, hygiene and other household messages, women men will be formed into nutrition care groups- mother-to-mother and father-to-father to enhance community-based management of acute malnutrition in the targeted communities of intervention. Further, caregivers will be strengthened and/or trained on family MUAC approach alongside community members including caregivers and PBWGs receiving quality GBV and PSEA messages. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtOutcome 3lt/bgt of the project strategically aimed to strengthen government-led health and nutrition systems including coordination, situation monitoring mechanisms to be capable to prevent and respond adequately to acute malnutrition issues in the targeted communities of intervention. Clearly, infrastructure of stabilization centres will be enhanced through additional bedding, OTP sites will be strengthened and provided with essential WASH materials and GBV risks mitigation messages. ltbrgtlt/pgt
